Restaurants & cafés.

Plan each area around its service window.

A leaking fitting behind the counter and a repair across the customer entrance affect the venue in different ways. We define the work area, the service interruption and the clean-up required before agreeing attendance. Small faults and larger refreshes receive their own scope.

01 / Paving beside outdoor seating

Front of house. Back of house. Outside.

Distinguish a loose threshold on the customer route from a leaking fixture or slow drain in the back of house. Reserve enough time for clean-up and returning equipment before service. If dining occupies public land, check the approved layout before moving seating or narrowing the pedestrian route.

  • Customer-facing areas

    We scope doors, walls, ceilings, lighting, amenities and fixed fittings. Visible finishes are checked for matching, and the customer route is considered alongside the repair.

  • Water and service areas

    Agreed water, hot-water and drainage faults are recorded by fixture and location. We identify the effect of isolating a service before work begins.

  • Outdoor dining

    We review the agreed paving, entrance, fixed items and drainage points with tables, deliveries and pedestrian movement in mind.

Agree the sequence with your manager

  1. 01

    Set the boundary

    We confirm the area available, nearby preparation or service activity and the nominated contact for access and decisions.

  2. 02

    Coordinate connected tasks

    Building repairs, plumbing, electrical work and final finishes are sequenced according to the agreed scope. Waste removal and cleaning are included in the plan.

  3. 03

    Check before reopening

    We record completed work and any material, testing or follow-up condition that remains before the affected area returns to normal use.

Maintaining outdoor dining areas ↗

Keep the outdoor layout in the brief

Map terrace tables, staff paths and shared delivery routes. Record when the surface is available for setting tables again.

For roadside dining on public land, the existing permitted layout and pedestrian clearances form part of the information to confirm. A private terrace needs its own site and property requirements checked. We identify which setting applies before defining the affected area.

We separate washing, a local paving repair and a change to drainage. Each has different access, material and waste-water arrangements; one task is not assumed to resolve the others.

  3. Clean and reopen
Outdoor dining

Details that help us define the work

  • The fault and the space

    Send the fixture or area, when the problem occurs, photographs and any known model or previous repair.

  • The venue timetable

    Include preparation and trading periods, deliveries, access restrictions and the areas that need to remain available.

Hand back by trading area.

We record the areas available for service, the routes in use and any outstanding drying or cleaning requirement.

A usable handover for the venue

We provide a record of completed items, the checks actually carried out and any agreed follow-up. Clean-up is confirmed against the work area, with remaining reopening conditions made clear to your manager.

Set protection, drying and clearing times separately for service counter and terrace work.

Common questions

Common questions

Can you work while part of the venue stays open?+

We assess whether the work area, customer route and affected services can be separated. The agreed plan identifies the area unavailable and any task that needs a different attendance window.

Can an outdoor puddle be fixed by cleaning the drain?+

We check the surface and accessible drainage route before setting the scope. Debris, a local surface defect and a downstream drainage issue call for different work.
